note: Platform-agnostic short-form baseline. Neither TikTok nor Instagram publishes a 'what is viral' API, so this is a documented starting point, not measured data. Ground it in real numbers with `viralforge trends analyze` (provider: file or apify).

hook_patterns: A flat contradiction of something the viewer believes: 'X is the worst advice in Y.'
A number with a stake attached: 'I lost $40,000 learning this.'
Name the viewer's exact situation in the first four words: 'If you're 25 and broke...'
Open mid-argument, no preamble - the first word is already the point
A question the viewer cannot answer but wants to: 'Why does nobody talk about this?'
Promise a specific, checkable payoff: 'By the end of this you'll know exactly when to quit.'
Confess something slightly costly to admit - specificity beats drama
Name a villain: the industry, the algorithm, the received wisdom
general.rubric: A clip travels when it is a complete thought that needs zero context, lands its most interesting sentence in the first three seconds, and gives the viewer something to do with it afterwards - repeat it, argue with it, or send it to one specific person. Length follows content: cut the moment the point is made. Density matters more than duration; a 45-second clip with no dead air outperforms a padded 25-second one.
general.caption_guidance: One line that adds to the video rather than describing it - a stake, a question, or the part you left out. Front-load the searchable words. No 'in this video I'. Emoji only where it carries meaning.
avoid: Cold opens that start mid-sentence with an unresolved pronoun ('...and that's why he did it')
Windups: 'so basically what I was saying is'
Clips that only make sense if you heard the previous five minutes
Inside jokes, guest names, or references with no setup
A payoff that lands after the viewer has already left - anything past 3s of setup
Generic advice with no specific number, name, or consequence

hook_patterns: Lead with the money: a revenue number, a loss, a price
Contradict the standard advice by name: 'Stop building an MVP.'
Name the mistake before the fix
Name the mistake the viewer is making right now
Before/after framing stated in the first sentence
'You don't need X' where X is what everyone sells
Start on the guest's most unguarded sentence, not the host's question
Open on disagreement between the two voices
A confession, stated plainly
State the counter-intuitive result first, explain second
'Nobody teaches this' + the specific thing
Pose the exam-style question, then answer it
Show the outcome first, then rewind
'This shouldn't be possible'
Name the stake: rank, streak, money
Start one beat before the punchline, never at the setup
Visual or tonal incongruity in frame one
The straight line delivered completely deadpan

notes: Captions are searchable - TikTok is used as a search engine, so the first words should be the query someone would type.
Keep the bottom ~18% and right ~14% of the frame clear of text: the UI sits there.
Reels favour rewatches and sends - a loopable ending is worth more than a sign-off.
Only the first ~125 characters show before 'more'.
The title doubles as the hook - it is visible before playback in feeds.
